title: Linear Equations — One Variable
description: Solve linear equations with one variable, including those requiring multiple steps.
objectives: Recognize equations with one, no, or infinitely many solutions

lessons.title: Multi-Step Equations
lessons.content: Combine like terms, distribute, then isolate the variable.

lessons.title: Special Cases
lessons.content: Some equations have no solution or infinitely many solutions.

title: Linear Equations — Two Variables
description: Graph and interpret linear equations in two variables.
objectives: Graph a line using slope and y-intercept
Interpret slope as rate of change

lessons.title: Slope-Intercept Form
lessons.content: y = mx + b, where m is slope and b is y-intercept.
examples: y = −x + 5: falls 1 for every 1 moved right

lessons.title: Slope as Rate of Change
lessons.content: Slope = rise/run = (y₂−y₁)/(x₂−x₁)

title: Systems of Equations
description: Solve systems of two linear equations by graphing, substitution, and elimination.

lessons.title: Graphing Method
lessons.content: Graph both lines; the intersection is the solution.
examples: Parallel lines: no solution; same line: infinitely many solutions

lessons.title: Substitution and Elimination
lessons.content: Algebraic methods give exact solutions.

title: Functions
description: Understand functions as input-output rules; compare linear and nonlinear functions.
objectives: Define a function; identify from tables and graphs

lessons.title: What is a Function?
lessons.content: A function assigns exactly one output to each input.
examples: (1,2),(1,5),(2,3) → NOT a function (1 maps to two outputs)
Vertical line test: if a vertical line crosses the graph twice, not a function

lessons.title: Linear vs. Nonlinear
lessons.content: Linear functions form straight lines; nonlinear do not.

title: Exponents and Scientific Notation
description: Apply properties of exponents; express very large/small numbers in scientific notation.
objectives: Apply product, quotient, and power rules for exponents
Convert to and from scientific notation

lessons.title: Exponent Rules
lessons.content: Laws of exponents simplify expressions.
examples: xᵃ · xᵇ = xᵃ⁺ᵇ: x³ · x⁴ = x⁷
xᵃ ÷ xᵇ = xᵃ⁻ᵇ: x⁶ ÷ x² = x⁴

lessons.title: Scientific Notation
lessons.content: Write as a × 10ⁿ where 1 ≤ a < 10.

title: Geometry — Transformations
description: Perform and describe transformations: translations, rotations, reflections, dilations.
objectives: Translate, rotate, and reflect figures on the coordinate plane
Identify congruence and similarity through transformations

lessons.title: Rigid Transformations
lessons.content: Congruence-preserving transformations: translations, rotations, reflections.

lessons.title: Dilations
lessons.content: Dilations change size but not shape (similarity transformation).
examples: Scale factor > 1: enlargement; between 0 and 1: reduction

title: Pythagorean Theorem
description: Understand and apply the Pythagorean Theorem in 2D and 3D.
objectives: State and prove the Pythagorean Theorem

lessons.title: The Theorem
lessons.content: In a right triangle: a² + b² = c² (c is the hypotenuse).

lessons.title: Distance Formula
lessons.content: Distance between two points = √((x₂−x₁)² + (y₂−y₁)²)

title: Volume of Curved Solids
description: Calculate volume of cylinders, cones, and spheres.
objectives: Use volume formulas for cylinders, cones, and spheres

lessons.title: Cylinder and Cone
lessons.content: Cylinder: V = πr²h. Cone: V = ⅓πr²h (one-third of cylinder).

lessons.title: Sphere
lessons.content: V = (4/3)πr³

title: Statistics — Bivariate Data
description: Analyze relationships between two variables using scatter plots and linear models.
objectives: Predict using a line of best fit

lessons.title: Scatter Plots
lessons.content: Plot paired data (x, y); look for patterns.
examples: Hours studied vs. test score: positive correlation
Temperature vs. hot chocolate sales: negative correlation
No pattern: positive correlation, negative correlation, or no correlation

lessons.title: Line of Best Fit
lessons.content: A trend line models the relationship; use it to predict.
examples: Line: y = 5x + 60; predict score for 8 hours: y = 5(8) + 60 = 100
Extrapolation (predicting beyond data range) can be unreliable

title: Introduction to Algebra — Quadratics Preview
description: Explore quadratic patterns and prepare for high school algebra.
objectives: Recognize quadratic patterns from tables and graphs
Understand the shape of a parabola

lessons.title: Quadratic Patterns
lessons.content: Quadratic functions grow faster than linear; their graphs are parabolas.
examples: Compare linear y=2x to quadratic y=x²: quadratic overtakes linear quickly

lessons.title: Evaluating Quadratics
lessons.content: Substitute x values to find y values for y = ax² + bx + c.
